meta.parties: Mackie Et Al. v. The Attorney General

rules.statement: The market value of shares, for estate duty purposes, should be based on the price a willing vendor and purchaser would reasonably expect, considering the nature of the business, risks involved, and any restrictions in the Articles of Association.
rules.supporting_quote: "In regard to valuation, for purposes of estate duty, of shares (not being preference shares) held by a deceased person in a Company at the time of his death in September, 1940 Held , (i) that the price which the willing vendor could reasonably expect to obtain and a willing purchaser could reasonably expect to have to pay for the shares in question is the measure of the value contemplated in section 20 (1) of the Estate Duty Ordinance."
